comments.text:
I think the following pattern would be useful:


> x <- rev(rep(6:10, 1:5))
> RLE <- rle(x)
> inverse.rle(RLE[2:4])

the idea being I've identified RLE components 2:4 of x as being useful and want to un-RLE them as a way to implicitly subset x.

Currently [ treats RLE like a list; my proposed method is simply

> `[.rle` = function(x, i) { structure(lapply(x, `[`, i), class='rle') }

(with some bells & whistles for consistency checks, and it should probably use oldClass, etc)

This is mildly backwards-incompatible (an `[[` method would be more troublesome), inasmuch as people rely on list indexing for rle objects, so I'm suggesting it here before putting in the work to file a patch.

A case could also be made that the RLE behave as its expanded vector equivalent. The Bioconductor package S4Vectors has an Rle object with rich functionality. It only supports subscripting into the expanded form; not the runs as you desire. 

Please give us more details on your use case, because this is the first time we've encountered this need.
 
Note that you could create a data frame with `as.data.frame.list()`, subset it by row, and then just inverse the encoding with `rep()`. That is roughly equivalent to the ranges-based workflow in S4Vectors/IRanges.

My use case is here:

https://gist.github.com/MichaelChirico/4568f11c8062b9bc7207f24aaffb6ce2#file-posix_java_switch-r-L71-L75

x is a (strsplit-by-character) POSIX-ish string like "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S Asia/Yangon".

The goal is to convert it to a Java SimpleDateFormat string like 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss 'Asia'/'Yangon'".

The "RLE subset" is helpful for escaping the 'Asia' and 'Yangon' substrings: once we get to the 'A' without a preceding '%', we go forward to the next non-numeric character ('/') and inverse-RLE that part to escape:

> if (grepl('[a-zA-Z]', ptn$values[jj])) { # needs to be escaped
>     JJ = jj
>     while (grepl('[a-zA-Z]', RLE$values[jj+1L])) JJ = JJ+1L
>     out[jj] = paste0("'", paste(inverse.rle(lapply(RLE, `[`, jj:JJ)), collapse = ''), "'")
>     jj = JJ+1L
> }


here lapply(RLE, `[`, jj:JJ) would be replaced by RLE[jj:JJ]

Looking again here, I'm reminded of Bug 17409 -- `POSIXlt` is another class where the default `[` / `[[` extractors just access the underlying list implementation, but something more abstract can be useful.

With that in mind, maybe the way to go here is to enable matrix notation in `[`, so that `RLE[, 2:4]` achieves the desired result, and is also fully back-compatible. It also maps well to how `print.rle` displays the object (it looks like selecting columns):

```
RLE
# Run Length Encoding
#   lengths: int [1:5]  5 4 3 2 1
#   values : int [1:5] 10 9 8 7 6
RLE[, 2:4]
# i.e., structure(lapply(RLE, `[`, 2:4), class='rle')
# Run Length Encoding
#   lengths: int [1:3] 4 3 2
#   values : int [1:3] 9 8 7
```

Created attachment 3809
`[.rle` path

Put together a quick patch to implement this functionality, along with updated documentation and tests.

New behavior:

```

x <- rev(rep(6:10, 1:5))
rle(x)
rx <- rle(x)
rx
## lengths [1:5]  5 4 3 2 1
## values  [1:5] 10 9 8 7 6

# Subsets lengths and values together
rx[2:4]
## lengths [1:3] 4 3 2
## values  [1:3] 9 8 7

# same as above
rx[, 2:4]

# subsets just "lengths"
rx["lengths", 2:4]
## [1] 4 3 2

# subsets just "values"
rx["values", 2:4]
## [1] 9 8 7
```

comments.text:
Thanks for the patch.

The matrix-style interface makes sense. I'd strongly recommend simplifying the contract to having the `i` always refer to either `lengths` or `values`. In other words, do not treat `i` as `j` when it is not lengths, values or 1. That should just error out.

The implementation could also be simplified by just calling `NextMethod(x=x, i=i)` after the guard against `i` being missing. Then just subset the result if `j` is present.
Actually, it is probably best to just do `unclass(x)[i]` instead of messing with `NextMethod()`.

comments.text:
Created attachment 3822
`[.rle` with decompress arg

Chatted offline with lawremi@, summarizing discussion

While we're here making changes, it might be nice to add support for indexing into the *decompressed* vector. This is a pretty natural thing to do want to do, and it's not a ton of additional work to add in support for.

Attaching a new patch that implements this functionality. This gives us the following methods to subset an `rle`:

```
> r <- rle(rep(seq_len(4L)-1L, times=seq_len(4L)))
Run Length Encoding
  lengths: int [1:4] 1 2 3 4
  values : int [1:4] 0 1 2 3

> r[1]
$lengths
[1] 1 2 3 4

> r["lengths"]
$lengths
[1] 1 2 3 4

> r[,2:3]
Run Length Encoding
  lengths: int [1:2] 2 3
  values : int [1:2] 1 2

> r["lengths",2:3]
$lengths
[1] 2 3

> r["lengths",2:3,drop=TRUE]
[1] 2 3

> r[1:4,decompress=TRUE]
[1] 0 1 1 2

> inverse.rle(r, subset=1:4)
[1] 0 1 1 2
```

This patch also includes more comments, better documentation, and more testing. I think this can supersede the previous version.
